summary: This article explains why the Moon seems to change shape during a month: it reflects sunlight, and as it orbits Earth we see different amounts of its lit half.
introduce: Write “Alike” and “Different” at the top of a T-chart on the board and ask students to compare two school subjects in one minute. Explain that “The Phases of the Moon” asks them to make the same kind of comparison.

keyTerms.def: a set of events that happens again and again in the same order
growing larger, used for the lit part of the Moon

challengeTerms.def: one half of a ball or sphere
having to do with the Moon

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that the Moon really changes its shape during the month? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Describe the Moon's cycle from one new Moon to the next.
struggling: Pre-teach illuminated, cycle, and waxing with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers fill in a T-chart of alike and different with sentence starters.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses hemisphere, lunar, and illuminate to compare two ideas from the article and explain which difference matters most.
